name: Ananias and Sapphira
charge: Lying to the Holy Spirit about a gift
summary: A couple sold property and gave part of the proceeds to the apostles while claiming it was the whole. The gift was never required; the lie was the offense. Each fell dead as it was exposed.
offense: They agreed together to keep back part of the price and present the rest as the full amount, a staged generosity meant to buy standing. Peter named it: not a lie to men but to God.
judgment: Ananias fell dead at Peter's word; Sapphira, questioned three hours later and holding to the same story, fell dead as well. Great fear came on the whole church.

entries.commentary: Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession and kept back part of the price, his wife being privy to it, and brought only a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet. This continues from Acts 4: none among the believers lacked, because those who possessed lands or houses sold them, laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man as he had need. The church was the epicenter of the community, where counsel was given and economic and community problems were resolved, the way the black Wall Street towns like Rosewood and Tulsa once kept the dollar circulating among our own people for months before it left. A community is a people with all things in common: common government, common heritage, common interest, and common culture, and the word community itself comes from the root "common." So-called black people today are not yet a community, divided by religion, politics, and color, until they come into the fullness of Christ. Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation. -

Peter asks why Satan has filled Ananias' heart to lie to the Holy Ghost and keep back part of the price; while it remained it was his own, so he has not lied unto men but unto the Most High. The spirit upon them was covetousness as well as lying; they saw the full value and coveted it, and did not put away lying as the renewed mind requires. To be renewed in the spirit of the mind is to be born again, to reboot the mind and clear out the programming of this world's philosophy, and to speak every man truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another. Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform. -

Hearing these words, Ananias fell down and gave up the ghost, and the young men wound him up, carried him out, and buried him. This is after the death of Christ, under grace, yet he was put to death for lying and breaking his vow. Grace was never a licence to sin; the wages of sin is death, even now. The christian church hands out a licence to sin by teaching the law is done away and all is covered by grace, and is answerable for the blood in the community when men sin presumptuously believing there are no consequences. Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure. -

About three hours later Sapphira came in, not knowing what was done, and agreed to the same lie; Peter told her the feet of those who buried her husband were at the door, and she fell down and yielded up the ghost and was buried by him, and great fear came upon all the church. She shared his fate because they agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Most High. A wife is meant to be a tower against death and a help meet; had she refused the evil or brought it to the leadership, she could have saved his life, as Abigail did. A wife submits to her husband as unto the Most High, in righteousness, not in wickedness; if he tells her to break the law, she is not to agree with him. Not everyone has the same measure of grace; one man is put to death for a smaller sin while David was spared far greater ones, for grace is given by the measure of the gift of Christ. The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him. -

By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were wrought; they were together in Solomon's porch, believers were the more added, and multitudes brought the sick into the streets on beds and couches that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow them, and they were healed every one. This is the power poured out after they waited in Jerusalem for the Holy Ghost, fulfilling that these signs would follow them that believe. These gifts of healing and tongues were for that time, to introduce the Son of God and prove the power of the Most High on earth; they are not the gifts of today, which is why our people still die of disease no matter what the pastors claim. In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established. -

The high priest and the sect of the Sadducees, filled with indignation, laid hands on the apostles and put them in the common prison, but the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night and sent them to stand and speak in the temple all the words of this life. Read the lives of the apostles and prophets as a pattern for today: what the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse; if you teach this gospel, prison and loss will come, so you cannot be joined to this world. Prepare for it: set aside a nest so your wife and family are provided for if you are locked up, for they will freeze accounts and take houses; the Most High will help, but you must still prepare. Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat. -

At dawn the apostles entered the temple and taught; when the council sent to the prison the officers found it shut with all safety and the keepers standing, but no man within, and word came that the men they had imprisoned were standing in the temple teaching the people. This is boldness: freed from prison, they did not hide but went straight back to teach. If they lock you up, go right back out, the way those who truly love their people keep returning no matter how many times they are jailed.

The captain and officers brought them without violence, fearing the people would stone them, and the high priest charged them, saying, did we not straitly command you not to teach in this name, yet you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine and intend to bring this man's blood upon us. It is the same charge leveled today: that teaching the truth fills the cities with this doctrine and tries to lay guilt on the accusers, the way they say teaching history is only meant to make them feel guilty.

Peter and the apostles answer that we ought to obey the Most High rather than men; the God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom they slew and hanged on a tree, and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. Christ came through the loins of David, from Judah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the law was given to Israel, so repentance from breaking the law is given to Israel. The apostles are his witnesses of these things because their lineage experienced his ministry, death, and miracles; popes and denominations are not witnesses. The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it. -

Cut to the heart, the council took counsel to slay them, no different from religious leaders today who take counsel against the truth, publish books against it, and would sooner hire accusers than correct themselves. Then Gamaliel, a Pharisee and a doctor of the law held in reputation among all the people, stood up and commanded the apostles to be put outside a little space. When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put the teachers to death thinking they do the will of the Most High. -

Gamaliel warns the council to take heed what they do: before these days Theudas rose up boasting himself to be somebody, and about four hundred joined him, but he was slain and his followers scattered to nothing; after him Judas of Galilee drew people in the days of the taxing and also perished, and his followers were dispersed. The record of Josephus tells the same of Theudas, a magician who persuaded a great part of the people that he was a prophet who could divide the river Jordan, until horsemen fell on them, killed many, and beheaded him; examine such men and see what their work comes to. Therefore refrain from these men and let them alone: if this counsel or work be of men it will come to nought, but if it be of the Most High it cannot be overthrown, lest they be found to fight against God. Examine our works the same way: if the teaching reforms the brothers off the streets and restores our people's identity worldwide, it is of the Most High; the more they persecute, lock up, and kill, the faster prophecy is filled toward the number to be sealed, so every move is checkmate.

The council agreed with Gamaliel, and when they had called the apostles and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus and let them go. The apostles departed rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name; that is the level to reach, to rejoice in the beatings, jail, and loss that come with the gospel. Daily in the temple and in every house they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ; this is the pattern, to teach every day on every platform, not once a week. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

verses.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.
And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.
And the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him.
And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.
And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much.
Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.
Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.
Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.
